title: Syncphony: Synchronized Audio-to-Video Generation with Diffusion Transformers
claim: Generation proceeds by iteratively denoising each new latent, conditioned on prior outputs, with text and audio injected through separate attention pathways.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right flow, green feedback loop arching over the top
description: A single-panel pipeline diagram reading left to right. On the left, a stack of previous latents (shown as dog photos) is concatenated with a gray noise image labeled z_l^T. A thick arrow leads to a diagram of a transformer backbone. Its gray, snowflake-marked frozen blocks sit on the left, and an orange-bordered, flame-marked trainable block sits on the right, with alternating green joint self-attention bars and peach audio cross-attention bars. The output is a denoised dog latent. A green arrow arches over the top and returns the output to the previous-latents stack, labeled auto-regressive generation. Below, a 'dog barking' text prompt feeds a frozen Text Encoder that connects to both blocks. An audio waveform feeds an Audio Encoder and then a trainable Audio Projector, which connects to the cross-attention layers. A legend at the lower right explains the layer colors.
caption: Overview of our video generation framework. Given an initial frame, a text prompt, and an audio waveform, the model autoregressively predicts each video latent through iterative denoising. At each timestep, it conditions on previously generated latents, while receiving multimodal guidance: text features via joint self-attention, and audio features via cross-attention. For brevity, latents are visualized as RGB frames, but they are spatiotemporal features extracted by VAE.
abstract: Text-to-video and image-to-video generation have made rapid progress in visual quality, but they remain limited in controlling the precise timing of motion. In contrast, audio provides temporal cues aligned with video motion, making it a promising condition for temporally controlled video generation. However, existing audio-to-video (A2V) models struggle with fine-grained synchronization due to indirect conditioning mechanisms or limited temporal modeling capacity. We present Syncphony, which generates 380x640 resolution, 24fps videos synchronized with diverse audio inputs. Our approach builds upon a pre-trained video backbone and incorporates two key components to improve synchronization: (1) Motion-aware Loss, which emphasizes learning at high-motion regions; (2) Audio Sync Guidance, which guides the full model using a visually aligned off-sync model without audio layers to better exploit audio cues at inference while maintaining visual quality. To evaluate synchronization, we propose CycleSync, a video-to-audio-based metric that measures the amount of motion cues in the generated video to reconstruct the original audio. Experiments on AVSync15 and The Greatest Hits datasets demonstrate that Syncphony outperforms existing methods in both synchronization accuracy and visual quality. Project page is available at: https://jibin86.github.io/syncphony_project_page
